message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s how you can quickly find the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow (US EPA)** | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), forecast, and health recommendations. | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> → “Find Air Quality” → type “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. |
| **AQICN (World Air Quality Index)** | Global coverage, real‑time AQI, historical data, and a mobile app. | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/> or download the app. |
| **Local news outlets** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily air‑quality summaries, especially during smog events. | Check their weather or environment sections. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Many include an AQI widget. | Search “Los Angeles AQI” in the app. |

### Quick Tips for Interpreting AQI

| AQI Range | Health Impact | Recommended Action |
|-----------|---------------|--------------------|
| 0–50 (Good) | No adverse health effects | Normal outdoor activities |
| 51–100 (Moderate) | Unhealthy for sensitive groups (children, elderly, people with respiratory issues) | Reduce prolonged outdoor exertion |
| 101–150 (Unhealthy) | Everyone may experience health effects | Limit outdoor activity, especially strenuous |
| 151–200 (Very Unhealthy) | Serious health effects | Avoid outdoor activity, consider indoor air purifiers |
| 201+ (Hazardous) | Health warnings of emergency conditions | Stay indoors, keep windows closed, use HEPA filters |

If you’re planning to be outside or have health concerns, it’s a good idea to check the AQI a few hours before you head out. Let me know if you’d like help interpreting a specific AQI reading or if you need tips on reducing indoor pollution!
